goal: Predict the human follows_feedback label on the annotation queue's labelled rows. Direction: MAXIMIZE F1 on the false class (the rows where the app ignored the user's feedback).
evaluators: F1 on the false class (label value == false, i.e. the app did NOT follow the user's feedback). Higher is better. Always reported alongside: confusion matrix, Wilson 95% CI on the headline, flip rate across runs, constant-class baseline, per-class recall and support, confidence calibration (mean confidence when right vs wrong, accuracy per band).
domain_notes: framing = grader: the judge sees the recommendation context AND the song the app chose, and predicts the human's pass/fail. The app's output is the object of judgement and is therefore legitimate evidence.

Forbidden in the judge's prompt at prediction time: the human's label or assessment, the reviewer's identity or timestamp, any reviewer reasoning text, and any prior evaluator verdict on the same trace (the traces carry goal-completeness, prompt-rule-violation, discovery, tool-retry-loop evaluations - all leakage).
A dataset expected_output is never ground truth here; only the human's value in the queue is. There is no expected_output on these rows anyway.
Never write a rule that names a specific row, artist or track from the corpus. That is memorisation, not a criterion. Changes must be general criteria a human reviewer would recognise.
A false verdict must be evidenced from the payload, not preferred. Equally, a judge that answers true everywhere scores 0.0 on this metric and has learned nothing.

The trace carries no genre, era or style field anywhere - not on the root span, not in the Spotify tool results. Deciding whether a recommendation belongs to a rejected genre is necessarily the judge's own music knowledge. Do not add prompt instructions that assume a genre field exists.

The strategist span's stated strategy is deliberately NOT in the payload: the human graded the song, not the plan. On row 10459dc6 the strategy announced a pivot to classic rock and the row was still labelled fail.
Rows with no verbatim Feedback quote were labelled true by the reviewer. The judge must handle 'no explicit constraint expressed' as a pass, not as missing information.
dataset_mode_note: Deviation from auto-experiment Step 1, recorded deliberately. (a) No val/test split: build-eval-from-annotations fixes no holdout below 40 usable rows, and this corpus has 13 - stratifying a 3-row class is arithmetic theatre. split_mode = all_rows, every score in-sample. (b) The corpus dataset write failed on this org: create_llmobs_dataset returned 500 once, then returned a success body for id 223ebfa5-2477-4f7c-ac3d-52f114d0aae2 which is not readable (404) or writable ('not found in project') afterwards. The harness reads .build_eval_from_annotations/corpus/rows.jsonl, whose source of truth is the annotation queue itself.

iteration_results.reasoning: KEPT - significant (delta vs best +0.1333, t=2.45, min_delta 0.02). Targeted the veto_resolved_in_the_app_s_favour census bucket: the judge was treating 'I do not recognise this as the vetoed genre' as evidence that it is not, so the prompt now puts the burden of proof on the pass whenever the user has vetoed a genre - a name, nationality, era or broad scene label is explicitly not enough, and the no-veto fallback is preserved verbatim. Mechanism audit PASSES: same 13-row denominator, 1 row gained (10459dc6), 0 lost, and the gained row is exactly the one the change targets. Read the significance carefully: it is arithmetically real but rests on a single row of a 3-row minority class, and the after-stdev (0.094) is far larger than the baseline stdev (0.0) that min_delta was derived from, so the 0.02 floor is optimistic. The gained row answered false in 2 of 3 full re-runs at confidence 55 - it sits on the judge's decision boundary rather than being settled. All scores in-sample; 13 rows, no holdout.

noise_calibration.derivation: min_delta = max(0.02, 0.5 * baseline_stdev) = max(0.02, 0.0) = 0.02. runs >= 8*(baseline_stdev/min_delta)^2 = 8*(0.0/0.02)^2 = 0, below the floor of 3, so runs stays at the pilot 3 and the baseline was NOT re-run. The judge scored 0.8 on all three full re-runs and flipped no row, so the metric is effectively deterministic at this corpus size; the 0.02 floor is what any keep must clear.
